thread:
incident-bot: Incident created: CUDA_OOM_SURPRISE at 1932102468
kai: heads up — alerts spiking for us-east-1 inference pool, multiple CUDA OOMs even though node headroom shows ~1.2GB free
maria: seeing same on 10 nodes, logs show allocator reserved blocks not being returned. stack traces point to cuMemAlloc failures with plenty of free headroom reported
ajay: is this the KV-cache / prefix cache change we shipped last week? any delta in config?
eng-runtime-lee: we pushed a change to prefer reserved blocks reuse, but there's a path that can pin blocks during paging -> fragmentation. collecting logs now
sre-arnold: moving traffic off affected nodes, starting drain for node-7a3
ops-bot: routing-rule update applied: route infer-us-east -> us-east-2 for 30m (by autoscaler)
kai: customer-impact: a few small customers saw 429s for ~2-3 minutes, CS notified
cs-olivia: notifying impacted tenant list; holding for root cause before broader comms
maria: paste logs:
```
E CudaAllocator: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory (caller=kv_cache::reserve_blocks)
W Runtime: headroom_report free_bytes=1.1GB reserved_bytes=2.4GB
D Allocator: free_slabs: 45 reserved_slabs: 230 pinned_slabs: 67
```
ajay: that pattern suggests reserved/slab mismatch — headroom calc didn't account for pinned_slabs, so free_bytes is misleading
eng-runtime-lee: reproducer: reduced memory churn locally by toggling KV_CACHE_EAGER_EVICT=true and forcing eviction of prefix cache; OOM goes away
eng-runtime-lee: workaround proposal: enable eager eviction on affected nodes and restart runtime; this will free pinned blocks but causes a short latency spike while cache warms
kai: agree. plan: 1) set KV_CACHE_EAGER_EVICT on node-7a3, node-8b2; 2) restart runtime process (graceful) 3) monitor OOMs and tail logs
sre-arnold: performing drain now: `kubectl cordon node-7a3 && kubectl drain node-7a3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
ops-bot: drain completed on node-7a3, pods moved
maria: live patch: exec into runtime pod and set env for new flag then restart container:
```
kubectl exec -n rwd runtime-pod-7a3 -- /bin/sh -c 'export KV_CACHE_EAGER_EVICT=1 && supervisorctl restart runtime'
```
eng-runtime-lee: did restart. initial logs show cache eviction loop freeing ~600MB of pinned slabs
maria: OOM counts dropped to 0 on those nodes. still seeing occasional reserve-failure traces on node-9c1
ajay: node-9c1 has a lot of fragmented allocations. propose to force spill->cpu for large tensors as temporary mitigation: set SPILL_POLICY=prefer_cpu on that node
kai: approved. apply and monitor
ops-bot: routing adjusted to send <10% residual traffic to nodes with spill_policy until stable
eng-runtime-lee: confirm: reserve accounting fix landed to master but needs canary; will roll a patch tomorrow to fix headroom calc; will open a hotfix PR if needed
maria: CS update drafted: short outage for small customers in us-east-1 due to OOMs caused by allocator fragmentation; mitigated via eviction and routing; no data loss
cs-olivia: sending out notice now
sre-arnold: followup items: - instrument reserved/pinned slabs in dashboards (maria) - add alert when reserved_bytes > headroom by >500MB (kai) - push canary for reserve-accounting fix (eng-runtime-lee) - write runbook step for KV cache eager-evict toggle (ajay)
kai: thanks everyone. marking incident resolved for now — re-open if OOMs resume
incident-bot: Incident resolved: duration 00:13:54, severity: sev2
